title: Relative functor categories for a Cartesian fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces, coherent functor categories and equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], Cartesian and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent cocartesian classification from [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Fix containing universes for all the following data. Let $p:Z\to B$ be a Cartesian fibration of small quasicategories, with coherent fiber transport $f^*:Z_{b'}\to Z_b$ for $f:b\to b'$. Let $C$ be a quasicategory in the containing universe. There is a cocartesian fibration $v:V_C\to B$ classified by the coherent functor $b\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(Z_b,C)$ and $f\mapsto(-)\circ f^*$. For every small simplicial set $T$ with map $t:T\to B$, the relative functor construction gives an equivalence of quasicategories
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{B}(T,V_C)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(T\times_B Z,C).$$
The left side is the quasicategory of functors over $B$ and coherent transformations over the identity on $t$. The equivalence sends $s$ to a functor whose restriction at a vertex $a\in T$ is the value $s(a):Z_{t(a)}\to C$. The equivalence is natural in $T$, in base change, and in $C$, including all higher simplices. For a cocartesian fibration $t:T\to B$, a functor $s:T\to V_C$ over $B$ preserves cocartesian edges if and only if its corresponding functor $T\times_B Z\to C$ sends every edge $(\eta,\epsilon)$, with $\eta$ a $t$-cocartesian edge and $\epsilon$ a $p$-Cartesian edge over the same base edge, to an equivalence. For an edge of $V_C$, the same test is applied after base change to its base edge $\Delta^1\to B$, taking the identity cocartesian fibration $T=\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$. The pullback above represents the infinity-categorical pullback since $p$ is a Cartesian fibration.

source.place: GHN Definition 7.2 and Proposition 7.3, dualized as in Corollary 9.9(2); cocartesian-edge criterion from HTT Corollary 3.2.2.13, explicitly unpacked in the proof of GHN Proposition 9.12. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Choose a universe containing $B,Z,C$ and all functor categories used below, and a further universe for $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Define $V_C$ in degree $n$ by pairs $(\sigma,h)$ with $\sigma:\Delta^n\to B$ and $h:\Delta^n\times_B Z\to C$; operators restrict both maps. Apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] with $S=B$, its Cartesian total category equal to $Z$, and $\mathscr A=C$. It states that this very simplicial object is a quasicategory, its projection $v$ is a cocartesian fibration, its fibre at $b$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(Z_b,C)$, and an edge is cocartesian precisely when its uncurried functor inverts the Cartesian edges of the edge pullback. Thus the data have been constructed degreewise, with their fibration and edge properties supplied by an existing theorem.

source.place: Definition 7.2, dual variance; HTT Corollary 3.2.2.13 specialized to a constant target

proof.text: For $t:T\to B$, apply the relative-Hom bijection of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] to $T\times\Delta^r$, mapped to $B$ through $t$. A map over $B$ from this object to $V_C$ is exactly a map $(T\times\Delta^r)\times_B Z\to C$. Reordering the last domain gives $(T\times_B Z)\times\Delta^r$. These are precisely the $r$-simplices of $\operatorname{Fun}_B(T,V_C)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(T\times_B Z,C)$, respectively, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Restriction along every simplex operator commutes with this reordering. We therefore have an isomorphism of simplicial sets, stronger than the asserted equivalence. Its right side is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], which applies to any small simplicial set as domain; hence its left side is one too. Restricting to a vertex $a$ gives exactly the functor $s(a):Z_{t(a)}\to C$. Taking $T=V_C$ and the identity over $B$ also constructs the universal evaluation $e:V_C\times_B Z\to C$.

source.place: Definition 7.2, relative-Hom formula with an arbitrary transformation parameter

proof.text: For $u:T'\to T$ over $B$, the two ways of applying the last bijection and restriction both send $H$ to $H\circ(u\times_B1_Z\times1_{\Delta^r})$. Postcomposing by $C\to C'$ likewise commutes with it. For a base map $a:B'\to B$ put $Z'=B'\times_B Z$. Over a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to B'$, both $a^*V_C$ and the relative exponential for $Z'\to B'$ have exactly the data $h:\Delta^n\times_B Z\to C$, with the same operators. Thus they are canonically isomorphic over $B'$. These identities commute with parameter simplices, and substitutions compose literally. This proves the claimed naturality in $T$, base change, and $C$, with all higher simplices.

The mapping-square theorem [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] converts horn-cocartesian edges to the intrinsic criterion assumed by the pointwise transport theorem. We compute transport as a functor, rather than only on objects. Fix $f:b\to b'$ and put $A=\operatorname{Fun}(Z_b,C)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$, with diagram shape $Z_{b'}^{\mathrm{op}}$, its fibre inclusion as source diagram, and the constant transformation $f^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing simplices gives a coherent Cartesian lift family $\lambda:Z_{b'}\times\Delta^1\to Z$ from $f^*$ to the fibre inclusion. Here ordinal reversal exchanges the initial and final horns in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Apply the same transport theorem to $v$, with shape $A$, its fibre inclusion, and the constant transformation $f$. This gives $L:A\times\Delta^1\to V_C$ with cocartesian interval edges, ending in a functor $f_!^v:A\to\operatorname{Fun}(Z_{b'},C)$. Pairing $L(F,t)$ with $\lambda(z,t)$ and applying $e$ gives a map $A\times Z_{b'}\times\Delta^1\to C$. At its endpoints it evaluates $F(f^*z)$ and $(f_!^vF)(z)$. Every interval edge is an equivalence by the edge criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential]. The componentwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore gives a natural equivalence $(-)\circ f^*\simeq f_!^v$, including all transformations in $F$ and $z$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3, dualized; agent universal-evaluation computation of transport

proof.text: For $\sigma:\Delta^n\to B$ put $Y=\Delta^n\times_B Z$. It is Cartesian by [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]. Apply opposite pointwise transport, justified by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], to $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ with shape $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the transformation from its projection to constant $0$ in $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$. It gives $R:Y\to Y_0$ and a Cartesian transformation $\iota R\to1_Y$ over $0\to i$. On $Y_i$, $R$ is transport along $0\to i$. Put $A=\operatorname{Fun}(Y_0,C)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $v_\sigma$ with shape $A\times\Delta^n$, source $(F,i)\mapsto(0,F)$ and base transformation $0\to i$. This gives $L:A\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to V_C$ with endpoint $W(F,i)$ and cocartesian interval edges. For $i\to j$, the square of $L$ has degenerate upper edge and cocartesian sides; its two triangles and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] imply that the lower edge is cocartesian. Pair $L(F,i,t)$ with the Cartesian lift $\lambda(y,t)$ of $0\to i$ for $y\in Y_i$ and apply $e$. This defines a map $A\times Y\times\Delta^1\to C$ with endpoints $F(Ry)$ and $W(F,i)(y)$. Each interval edge is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential], since its $V_C$ edge is cocartesian and its $Z$ edge Cartesian. Currying and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] give a coherent natural equivalence of these two $A\times Y$ diagrams. Restricting to $A\times Y_i$ identifies $W(-,i)$ with precomposition by $R|_{Y_i}$ on every transformation simplex.

source.place: Proposition 7.3, simplexwise comparison; agent parameterized lift argument

proof.text: For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, restricting the preceding construction replaces transport from $0$ by transport first from $0$ to $\theta(0)$ and then within $\sigma\theta$. The successive-transport clause of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] compares their composite with the restricted transport. These comparisons can be made coherently relative to their boundaries. Indeed [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-arrow-projection] gives a trivial Kan fibration from cocartesian lifts to base arrows with prescribed sources; every vertex is liftable here. Apply it also to the functor-category fibrations supplied by pointwise transport. For the Cartesian lifts use their opposites, prescribing targets. Induct on parameter-simplex dimension: fix the degenerate lift data by restriction; on each nondegenerate simplex its already chosen faces give the boundary upstairs, while the prescribed base transformation and source diagram give the simplex downstairs. Boundary lifting extends the family with those exact faces. It also extends comparisons between lift families by including their comparison parameter. Thus the two composite transports on a triangle have a compatible comparison, and every higher simplex extends its already fixed comparisons on all faces. Applying the single evaluation $e$ to these families gives compatible equivalences from Step 5; precomposition on the other side is the coherent internal-Hom operation of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. Hence the entire transport diagram is $b\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(Z_b,C)$ with $f\mapsto(-)\circ f^*$. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] this identifies the classifier of $v$, including higher simplices. Applying its contractible classification-choice clause to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ identifies any initially specified coherent transport with the lift model used here.

source.place: Proposition 7.3 and its dual as used in Corollary 9.9(2); agent coherent lift comparison

proof.text: Let $t:T\to B$ be cocartesian and let $H:T\times_B Z\to C$ correspond to $s$ under Step 2. For a $t$-cocartesian edge $\eta:a\to a'$, restrict $s$ and $H$ along $\eta$. The relative-exponential edge criterion says that $s(\eta)$ is $v$-cocartesian exactly when $H$ sends to equivalences all edges of the pullback $\Delta^1\times_B Z$ which are Cartesian over $\Delta^1$. Pullback stability and detection in [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] identify these with the edges whose $Z$-coordinate is $p$-Cartesian. Over the nondegenerate edge of $\Delta^1$ they are precisely the pairs $(\eta,\epsilon)$ in the statement. Over either constant endpoint, a Cartesian edge is an equivalence in the fibre: its opposite is cocartesian over an identity, and the mapping-square criterion in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] says that precomposition by it is an equivalence for every test object; testing its source and target gives an inverse. Functors preserve the inverse-triangle witnesses, so these endpoint edges automatically map to equivalences. Therefore the nondegenerate pairs give exactly the required test. Applying it to every $\eta$ proves both directions of cocartesian preservation. For a single edge of $V_C$, use the identity cocartesian fibration of $\Delta^1$ over the base edge; Step 3 gives the required base-change identification.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 9.12, the paragraph explicitly unpacking HTT Corollary 3.2.2.13

proof.text: For quasicategorical $T$, the strict pullback in the statement represents the infinity-categorical one. Indeed [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration] applies to Cartesian fibrations as well and makes $p$ a Joyal fibration. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](1) it is an isofibration of quasicategories. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] to $p$ and $t$: it identifies the degreewise square with a pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, tested on cores of all functor categories. No fibration condition on $t$ is needed.

source.place: HTT categorical-fibration pullback convention; agent application of the existing strict-pullback theorem

proof.text: If $T$ is merely a simplicial set, interpret its infinity category by a Joyal fibrant presentation. Factor $t$ as $T\xrightarrow{j}\widetilde T\to B$ with $j$ a trivial cofibration and the second map a fibration, using [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Since $B$ is fibrant, so is $\widetilde T$. The opposite $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cocartesian. Categorical equivalences are invariant under ordinal reversal: the degreewise identity $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},D)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K,D^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ converts the defining $h\operatorname{Fun}(-,D)$ tests into each other, and reversing inner horns shows $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ quasicategorical. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-categorical-base-change] to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $j^{\mathrm{op}}$, then reverse back. It follows that $T\times_B Z\to\widetilde T\times_B Z$ is a categorical equivalence. Step 8 identifies the latter with the infinity-categorical pullback of the presented objects. Thus the former is a simplicial presentation of the same pullback. The simplicial isomorphism of Step 2, and hence the asserted section equivalence, was already valid for arbitrary $T$ before this interpretation.

source.place: Definition 7.2; agent extension of the pullback interpretation to arbitrary simplicial parameters
